written.myAnswer: An enzyme is a biological catalyst that speeds up metabolic reactions without being consumed.
The active site is the region of an enzyme where its specific substrate binds. Its shape and chemical properties allow the enzyme to act specifically on that substrate.

Enzymes are biological catalysts, mostly globular proteins, with specific active sites. They act on particular substrates, are not consumed in reactions, and may require cofactors. They function in cells or outside them and can be used in industrial processes.
